newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech support for EU membership rises - poll.
newsitem.headline: Czech support for EU membership rises - poll.

text.p: Czech support for European Union (EU) membership has risen in recent months but remains well below levels of three years ago, according to an opinion poll released on Wednesday.
The poll taken by the state-funded IVVM institute in early November showed that 51 percent of respondents supported Czech membership in the EU compared with 42 percent in March.
But in a similar poll taken in May 1993, 66 percent of respondents supported the Czech Republic's EU membership, with only 12 percent against the idea, IVVM said.

Scepticism about the benefits of EU membership has grown among Czechs in recent years and conservative Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, who handed over Prague's application to join in January this year, has often criticised the red tape in Brussels.
Citizens of several other EU hopefuls, notably Poland and Romania, are much more enthusiastic about membership.

The latest poll actually shows opposition to EU membership, for which the Czech Republic is tipped as a front-runner among former communist countries, has also risen to 26 percent as of early November, compared with 21 percent in March.
